title: Worth money or a decision this week
lead: Five items where the value is clear and the cost is small.
rows: Buy it. Check the free companion repo first, and confirm the commercial licence covers client deliverables rather than just your own products.

Best new find. Copies real app screens into Figma as editable layers, with a Claude MCP connection for redesigning them. Set a house rule that output gets fully restyled before it goes anywhere near a client deliverable.
Publish one kit per retained client: their npm component package, published library variables, guidelines.md. Treat the kit as a delivery artefact.
Trial on an internal project only. Public Alpha with no Figma round-trip, so do not put it on a client deadline.
Use free browsing as a benchmarking reference. Get the Pro price in writing before wiring MCP into a workflow. Do not use extracted systems as a shortcut for a client brand.

title: Read once this week, then act
lead: Reference material with a specific follow-on action.
rows: Seven customisation mechanisms, chosen by trading context cost against authority: CLAUDE.md, path-scoped rules, skills, subagents, hooks, output styles, --system-prompt.
Audit the .claude/ setup for Foundry and client repos. Move bloated CLAUDE.md content into path-scoped rules and on-demand skills.
Model and effort are separate dials. High effort is roughly 7x the tokens of low on the same prompt.
Set a house default: mid-tier model at medium for routine build work, top model at high or max only for architecture, migrations and debugging.
~150 tools curated specifically for web design engineers. The only directory on the list with credible taste.
Read once, diff against the studio stack, record adoptions in the Foundry wiki. Do not bookmark and return — it has no update date.
On-device face grouping and video highlight detection above Vision. No Simulator support, and confidence scores are not exposed.
File it. When a client asks for "AI photo features" in a mobile brief, this is the answer — and the reason you cannot promise identity verification.
$3,600 Vercel credit over 12 months. Requires an actively maintained OSS project on Vercel with a published Code of Conduct.
Applications said they reopen in August, so re-check now. Only worth it if you open-source something real, and it creates a maintenance obligation.

title: Potential to build ourselves
lead: Ranked by strategic value, not ease. Column E is my read on whether it is worth your time.
rows: Point it at a live URL, pull computed colours, type scale, spacing and component patterns, emit Foundry token JSON plus a DESIGN.md for agents.

Feeds Foundry's existing design-system tab directly, and doubles as a pitch artefact - 'here is your current site's design system, extracted' is a good discovery deliverable. Do not copy Refero's catalogue; build the extractor for client sites only.
Schema-constrained generative UI bound to Foundry tokens
An LLM emits a constrained component contract rather than free-form HTML; your whitelisted, token-bound components render it. Prototype against one Foundry surface first.

This is the pattern with the longest shelf life on the list. If AI-generated interfaces have to render inside a client's design system rather than generic Tailwind, whoever owns that contract owns the handoff. Prototype, do not productise yet.
Watch the agency inbox, classify enquiries, draft replies from templates, escalate anything ambiguous to a human, log the lead against a Foundry client record.
Cheapest win on the list and it is internal, so no client risk. Build against your own stack, not the PDF's Make recipe.
Compress large agent-generated diffs into a conceptual reading diff before human review, wired into pull requests.
Try the existing Apache-2.0 tool before writing anything. The only asset is prompt quality. Verify model cost on large diffs before it goes near CI.
Weekend build - but use theirs first
Ambient status display for Foundry monitors
A Foundry dashboard view designed for an always-on screen - uptime monitors, Pulse scan results, live client status - on a cheap wall tablet.
Skip the custom firmware entirely. A responsive web view on a tablet gets nearly all the value. Nice studio artefact, mild client-confidence value if visitors see it.
Studio vetted-tools page in Foundry wiki
Your own curated, dated, opinionated list of tools the studio actually uses, with why and for what - in the Foundry wiki so it survives staff turnover.
Low effort, compounding value, and it is the right response to every public directory on this list: mine them once, keep your own record.
PDF CV in, templated one-page site out, on your design system and deploy pipeline.
Technically easy, commercially pointless. A $10/mo commodity market against Framer, Bento, Super and LinkedIn. Listed only so it is explicitly ruled out.

title: Follow, do not evaluate
rows: Official Anthropic account for developers — changelogs, Claude Code releases, API updates. The primary first-party feed for changes that could break Foundry tooling. Docs changelog is still the authoritative source for breaking changes.
Default React Native toolchain; SDK cadence dictates upgrade work on every app you ship. For incident signal follow @expo_status instead — @expo is the marketing feed.
Marketing feed for Wonder. Follow to see whether the alpha matures. Folded into the Wonder row on the Freemium tab.

High-signal on Claude Code practice. The specific post you linked could not be read — open it manually. Their early-August post about removing ~80% of the Claude Code system prompt is probably the more useful one.
Leon Lin — How To Actually Design With AI
Could not be read. Engagement-oriented design-Twitter content, so treat as inspiration not authority. Read it yourself before acting on it.
Could not be read and the account could not be identified at all — searches returned nothing. Paste the text or a screenshot if you want it assessed.

title: Park it
lead: Low value for Gitwork. Recorded so you do not re-research them.
rows: Not a motion library despite the name — it renders pre-baked video and sprite sheets, so it is heavy, non-responsive and not screen-reader accessible. Specialist hero-moment asset generator only. Keep GSAP or Motion for real UI animation, and budget the per-render AI video spend into the quote.
$144/yr for iOS screens plus revenue data. Overlaps Flaude. Only justified if you do real native iOS work.

Free and genuinely handy for case-study hero shots. Use the in-browser version — the max-quality export needs a Chrome extension downloaded as a raw ZIP with page-capture permissions, which does not belong on a machine holding client work.
Nice reference manager, but macOS only, no cloud sync, no team sharing, and "free" is a beta state with pricing unannounced. Do not build a team process on it yet.
$19 once for a local-Markdown daily work log. Fine personally; Foundry already owns the multi-user version of this.
Thin consumer directory. Worth stealing two things: the $100-for-30-days featured-listing model, and the submission form field spec if you ever build a showcase in Foundry.

Name reads like an accessibility tool. It is not — it is iPhone-to-Mac remote control. It will not help with WCAG audits in any way. No published pricing, and its AI assistant executes tasks on your Mac.
Dock launcher cosmetics. Only interesting as a design-craft and pricing-ladder reference.
Solo-operator SEO/affiliate directory. Depth is a sentence per tool. One real angle: listing Foundry there is cheap lead-gen.
Consumer Mac gear curation, same operator. Bookmark for hardware research, nothing more.
Bottom-of-market CV site builder. Mild commodity-pressure signal if you ever quote cheap one-pagers.
Thin wrapper around Flux on Together AI. Bitmap output, no SVG, and trademark risk you should not pass to a client.
No licence, no team, no component count published. No licence means no clear right to ship in client work. Transitions.dev is the serious option.
Useful for showreels, but pre-revenue indie signals — lifetime tier, quarterly-only billing. Fine for marketing output, not a client-facing dependency.
Hobby ESP32 hardware. Worth reading for code taste; the reusable bit is the Cloudflare Worker voice relay pattern.
6 stars, single author, early prototype, needs specific hardware and a Mac. Idea only — see build candidate 5.
Home Assistant plumbing. One lesson worth keeping: WebRTC that works in Safari can still fail inside an app webview, and codec negotiation is usually why.
Beginner-level newsletter lead magnet with a course upsell. The idea is worth more than the document — see build candidate 3.
Pre-launch landing page selling a $49 lifetime licence for an app that is not shipping. No App Store listing, no track record. Consumer, single-user, no agency angle.
GPU API reference for engine and graphics engineers. You will never write Metal on client work.
